# Saved source normal fixtures

These fixtures are generated by this repository's
[generate_normals.py](../generate_normals.py), not contributed assets or copied
Blender source. They are redistributable test data under the repository's
[license](../../../LICENSE). Blender runs only as a separate fixture-generation
and verification process.

All are uncompressed, normal-save files with one active Scene named `Normals`,
source unit scale `0.01`, and one Mesh Object named `Smooth`, `Flat` or `Split`.
File-browser directories are set to `//` before saving; generator regression
tests reject Windows absolute UI/home paths. No geometry is evaluated through
modifiers, shape keys, animation or custom normals.

## Geometry cases

Each Mesh combines independent pieces using distinct vertex indices. There
are 15 cases, 41 polygons and 137 corners per Blender version:

| Fixture | Points / faces / corners | Cases, in stored order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `smooth.blend` | 36 / 19 / 65 | unequal-angle wedge; same-direction shared edge; nonmanifold shared edge; disconnected vertex fans; open boundary fan; closed rectangular cube; concave polygon |
| `flat.blend` | 4 / 2 / 6 | flat unequal-angle wedge |
| `split.blend` | 35 / 20 / 66 | sharp-edge wedge; mixed flat/smooth wedge; same-direction shared edge; nonmanifold shared edge; disconnected vertex fans; internally split open fan; mixed flat/smooth cube with sharp edges |

The smooth Mesh has no true sharp-face/edge values, so Blender uses
angle-weighted point normals even for disconnected and nonmanifold geometry.
The split Mesh contains true sharp-face/edge values; Blender separates fans
at sharp, flat, boundary, nonmanifold and same-direction boundaries. These
cases distinguish domain selection from always averaging points or always
splitting manifold fans.

## Oracle format and validation

Each adjacent `.oracle.txt` is generated from Blender's source `vertices`,
`polygons`, `loops` and `corner_normals`, then compared again after reopening
the saved file. It contains:

1. The format marker `BLEND_NORMALS_ORACLE 1`.
2. Blender's version string.
3. Saved source unit scale and object count.
4. A quoted Mesh name followed by point, face and corner counts.
5. One source-space position vector per point.
6. Face corner counts on one line, then corner vertex indices on one line.
7. One source-basis normal vector per corner.

`blendScene.normals` independently reads the unchanged files through
`blendFile` and `DecodeScene`. It compares meter/basis-normalized positions,
unchanged topology and basis-rotated corner normals. Vector components use
absolute `2e-5` tolerance; native corner normals must have unit length within
`1e-12`. Reversing block records must preserve all Mesh arrays exactly.
These CTests run without Blender.

The generator's `--check` compares fresh and saved oracles using
`math.isclose(rel_tol=2e-6, abs_tol=2e-6)` without rewriting stored files.
Independent runs reproduce semantic oracles, not full-file bytes: saved
addresses and UI state may vary. See the
[build guide](../../../docs/guides/building.md#saved-normal-oracles) for
generation/check commands and
[test_generate_normals.py](../test_generate_normals.py) for regression checks.

## Boundary limitations

A generated 5.2.2 multi-Mesh prototype contained repeated saved addresses for
`Attribute` blocks and was rejected by `BLEND_POINTER_DUPLICATE`. These
fixtures deliberately use one Mesh per file; they do not establish general
multi-Mesh compatibility or relax the reader's exact-address uniqueness
contract. The prototype is not part of the committed corpus; investigation
remains in [task 2.5](../../../docs/roadmap/current.md).

This is source normal/mesh decoding evidence, not a custom-normal decoder,
Blender evaluation backend, Mesh transform oracle, USD-authored stage or
STAGE-O1's four-scale cube evidence. Current capabilities belong to the
[capability matrix](../../../docs/reference/CAPABILITY_MATRIX.md#5-scene-ir).
